scope: Read-only independent review of frozen fresh-plan batch utility, author probe, and exact post-receipt crash regression. Reviewer did not run tests or probes.
findings: Batch admission uses the existing dispatcher lock, authenticates the history once through entries(), validates the fixed roster before writes, and records its source/store/plan pins in durable intent. Per-plan admission receipt formats and executor dispatch/reconciliation semantics are unchanged.

The exact post-receipt crash regression demonstrates that ordinary enqueue preserves the receipt pin and tick reconstructs missing job scaffolding. The test stops at bind and asserts prepare/launch are not called; it launches no executor job.
Interrupted batch admission is a committed prefix and is intentionally not resumable through the batch tool. README directs recovery through ordinary enqueue and makes no atomic-batch claim.

Historical receipt trust retains the existing queue.entries boundary: admission fields and receipt-to-plan pin are checked, but there is no independent root signature that detects coherent replacement of both receipt and plan by an external writer. This is pre-existing queue behavior and the cooperative-lock limitation is documented.

The author probe reports 250 fixed independent plans: batch 4.6851 seconds with one history scan versus ordinary enqueue 8.1691 seconds with 250 scans; both report zero launches. This is one synthetic matched run over two fresh stores, with no repeated trials or uncertainty estimate. No 1000-plan run was observed or reviewed.
limitations: Evidence covers bounded admission of already known independent synthetic plans only.
No adaptive sequential cycles, model execution, scientific comparisons, production store, dispatch throughput, or 1000-plan probe were evaluated.
Existing status and dispatch still scan historical queue state.
